title: Confirmation of complex non-collinear Fe(II) spin ordering in the iron oxychalcogenide La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ by broad range $^{139}$La-NQR
authors: Tillmann Weinhold, Jerin Abraham George, Cornelius Herrmann, Domenic Nowak, Rajib Sarkar, Felix Seewald, Rowena Wachtel, Sabine Wurmehl, Bernd Büchner, Hans-Henning Klauss
abstract: The transition metal oxychalcogenide La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ exhibits a non-collinear spin-ice like antiferromagnetic ordering below $T_N \approx $ 90 K due to complex magnetic exchange interactions and axial single-ion anisotropy of Fe$^{2+}$ spins. The magnetic structure was deduced/determined from combined $^{57}$Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy and $^{139}$La-NMR on polycrystalline specimen. In this work, we present zero-field $^{139}$La-NQR investigations on polycrystalline La$_2$O$_2$Fe$_2$OSe$_2$ in a broad frequency and temperature range between 2.8 - 20 MHz and 4.2 - 100 K. The measured resonances at $ν_Q$, $2 \, ν_Q$, and $3 \, ν_Q$ are fully consistent with the previous NMR studies and also with the magnetic structure. A substantial modification of the electric field gradient at the La-position below $T_N$ is inconsistent with the current investigations.
summary: This work uses zero-field $^{139}	ext{La-NQR}$ spectroscopy to confirm the complex non-collinear antiferromagnetic spin ordering in La2O2Fe2OSe2 below 90 K. By analyzing the temperature dependence of the NQR resonances, the authors confirm the magnetic structure deduced from other techniques, providing detailed spectroscopic evidence of the magnetic interactions in this correlated material.
main_problem: To confirm the complex non-collinear Fe(II) spin ordering in the iron oxychalcogenide La2O2Fe2OSe2 using zero-field NQR measurements.
main_result: The measured NQR resonances are fully consistent with the proposed non-collinear magnetic structure, confirming the magnetic ordering below T_N. The analysis rules out significant changes in the electric field gradient at the La-site below T_N.
method: Zero-field $^{139}	ext{La-NQR}$ measurements were performed across a broad temperature and frequency range, comparing results with previous Mössbauer and NMR data.
model_or_system: The physical system is the transition metal oxychalcogenide La2O2Fe2OSe2, which exhibits spin-ice like antiferromagnetic ordering due to Fe2+ spin interactions. The analysis uses a Hamiltonian framework to model the interaction between the nuclear quadrupole moment and the local magnetic field.

main_assumptions: The magnetic field at the La_1 site is assumed to be much smaller than the field at the La_2 site, and the temperature dependence of the hyperfine field is proportional to the magnetic field at the iron position.

paper_structure: The paper establishes the magnetic background and then presents the NQR measurements, showing consistency with the magnetic structure. It then uses detailed simulations based on the Hamiltonian to analyze the temperature dependence of the resonance peaks, confirming the magnetic field parameters at different La sites.
why_interesting: The use of NQR spectroscopy to probe subtle changes in the local electronic environment induced by complex magnetic ordering in a Mott insulator is highly relevant for understanding emergent quantum states in correlated materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 2: Magnetic structure of La2O2Fe2OSe2 as determined by G¨unther et al. [9] and McCabe et al. [16]. The atoms are colored as in Figure 1. Red arrows indicate the direction of iron moments below TN. Black arrows at the La sites indicate the direction of the dipolar magnetic field ⃗B at the La positions induced by the iron moments. Two different La sites are present in the ordered phase due to different magnetic field strength and direction. These La sites are labeled as La 1 and La 2, consistent with the labeling by G¨unther et al. [9] and Hussain et al. [17].

FIG. 3: 139La NQR spectra of La2O2Fe2OSe2 at different temperatures. The base line of each spectrum is shifted by a factor that reflects the evolution of temperature. The dashed gray horizontal line marks the ordering temperature of TN ≈90 K. The open circles mark the peak positions of the NQR signals found by Hussain et al. [17]. The dashed bright orange and dark orange lines indicate the expected peak positions according to the model described in section IV. and introduced by G¨unther et al. [9] for site La 1 and La 2, respectively.

FIG. 4: Simulation of the NQR resonance positions for the case of a magnetic field being (a) parallel to the main component of the EFG corresponding to site La 2 in Figure 2 and (b) perpendicular to the main component of the EFG corresponding to site La 1 in Figure 2. Parameters used are νQ = 3.147 MHz and γ139La = 6.06 MHz T−1. The relative intensities of the various resonance peaks (color-coded as in the vertical bars) have been approximated by calculating the peak intensities for 2000 random orientations of the rf excitation pulse. Dashed black lines indicate the strength of magnetic field expected at the specified temperature.

FIG. 5: Local magnetic hyperfine field BHyp at the 57Fe position measured by M¨ossbauer spectroscopy. Black upwards facing triangles are data published by G¨unther et al. [9]. Grey downwards facing triangles are measured on the sample used in this work. The red line corresponds to a phenomenological order parameter function (see text).
